name: Poland
description: Poland from the baptism of 966 and the Commonwealth to partition, the World Wars, the Holocaust, communism, Solidarity and the European Union.

checkpoints.name: The Piast kingdom
checkpoints.note: Mieszko I was baptised in 966. The Piast kings ruled from Kraków and rebuilt after the Mongol raid of 1241.

checkpoints.name: The Commonwealth
checkpoints.note: A royal marriage joined Poland and Lithuania, which beat the Teutonic Knights at Grunwald. The Commonwealth became one of Europe's largest states, Copernicus moved the Earth, and Sobieski saved Vienna, before neighbours carved it up.

checkpoints.name: Partition and rebirth
checkpoints.note: For more than a century Poland was ruled by Russia, Prussia and Austria, and its people rose again and again. Chopin and Marie Curie made their names abroad, and Poland was reborn in 1918.

checkpoints.name: War and communism
checkpoints.note: Germany and the Soviet Union invaded in 1939. Millions of Poles, among them most of its Jews, were murdered, Warsaw was destroyed, and a Soviet-backed regime ruled until Solidarity rose.

checkpoints.name: Free Poland
checkpoints.note: The round table of 1989 ended communist rule. Poland joined NATO and the European Union and became one of Europe's fastest growing economies.
